summary_responses.response: The paper proposes DiffTry, a lightweight mechanism that prevents retry storms and protects high-value transactions when independently scaled microservices become overloaded. DiffTry assigns class-specific retry limits, allowing high-priority requests more attempts while restricting low-priority and potentially malicious traffic without requiring overload detection or service coordination. The authors develop analytical models for a two-service system and general microservice networks to estimate per-service and end-to-end rejection rates, prove convergence and monotonicity, and identify conditions guaranteeing unique solutions. Simulations, numerical experiments, and a live Kubernetes deployment show that DiffTry substantially reduces high-priority rejection rates while limiting resource use and matching the predicted behavior. Overall, the results indicate that selective retry budgets can provide scalable, coordination-free prioritization against both incidental overloads and adversarial traffic.

Under overload with DiffTry, high-priority requests achieve a rejection rate of around 15% and account for about 85% of successful completions when both classes contribute 50% of input load.

summary_responses.response: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) issued a direct final rule updating 5 CFR part 630 to align its Family and Medical Leave Act regulations with legislation enacted in January 2021 and December 2023. The revisions clarify that virtually all civilian federal service, including temporary or intermittent service, counts toward the 12-month service requirement for FMLA eligibility, although employees must still meet other eligibility criteria to use leave. They also allow certain honorable active-duty military service to count toward that requirement and permit annual or sick leave earned under laws outside Title 5 to be substituted for unpaid FMLA leave. The rule updates related paid parental leave eligibility provisions and excludes Veterans Health Administration employees covered under 38 U.S.C. 7421 from Title 5 FMLA coverage, reflecting their separate VA leave regime. It will take effect December 14, 2026, unless significant adverse comments are received by November 16, 2026, in which case OPM may withdraw affected provisions and issue a proposed rule.
